text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright dismissed tough Russian criticism of NATO enlargement ahead of the Helsinki summit as unimportant "rhetoric" on Thursday.
Accompanying U.S. President Bill Clinton for his summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, Albright said that what counted was the talks between the two leaders.
Asked by reporters about strong attacks on NATO enlargement from Russian officials, she said: "I think we have a lot of work to do...rhetoric leading up to the summit is not what is important".
Albright met Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen after arriving in Helsinki on Thursday.
On Wednesday, Russian presidential spokesman Sergein Yastrzhembsky said NATO's planned eastward expansion would be the West's biggest mistake since the end of the Cold War.
